ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the right-angled triangle $ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle ABC=30^\circ$. Three squares are constructed externally on the sides AC, BC, and AB of $\triangle ABC$, and the areas of these three squares are denoted as $S_1$, $S_2$, and $S_3$, respectively. Given that $S_1=9$, what is the value of $S_3$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Since $S_{1}=AC^{2}=9$, it results that $AC=3$. In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $\angle ABC=30^\circ$, hence $AB=2AC=6$. Therefore, $S_{3}=AB^{2}=\boxed{36}$.
